title: Gone with the Wind
synopsis: Tara, Georgia, 1861. War is coming. You are Scarlett, sharp and impossible. The man you want isn't the man who wants you.

nodes.text: Barbecue. Ashley announces his engagement to Melanie.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Spirit.
“Smile through it” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Strategy.

nodes.text: You tell Ashley you love him. Rhett, behind the couch, hears.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Spirit.
You commit to “Storm out.” The story records the instinct as “Pride” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: He bows. He says you're not a lady. He has noticed you.

choices.consequence: “Snap back” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Spirit.
You commit to “Walk away.” The story records the instinct as “Pride” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You marry Charles to spite Ashley. Charles dies of pneumonia.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Mourn correctly” back. Society shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Skip mourning.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You move to Atlanta. The hospitals fill. Rhett finds you again.

choices.text: Dance with him at the bazaar
choices.consequence: “Dance with him at the bazaar” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Spirit.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Yankees near. Atlanta burns. You deliver Melanie's baby.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Stay with her.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.
“Try to flee” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Survive.

nodes.text: Rhett finds a wagon. He drives you out of the city.

choices.consequence: “Trust him” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Path.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Spirit—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: He leaves you to join the army. You drive on alone.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Spirit—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Be grateful” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Mother dead. Father broken. The fields untended.

choices.consequence: “Rebuild” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Vow.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Honest.

nodes.text: You eat a radish in the field. As God is your witness.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Vow” back. Iron shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.

nodes.text: You marry your sister's fiancé to save Tara.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Iron.
There is no taking “Pretend to be a wife” back. Cover shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You are attacked on the road. Frank rides to avenge you.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Warn him not to.” The story records the instinct as “Wise” and carries it forward.
“Let him go” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.

nodes.text: Frank dies in the raid. You wear black again.

choices.consequence: “Be honest with yourself” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Truth.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Survival—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: He proposes. You accept for security.

choices.consequence: “Marry him” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Practical.
There is no taking “Wait” back. Heart shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: New Orleans. Lavish. He is, briefly, tender.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Notice.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Take it for granted” back. Spoiled shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Your daughter. He adores her.

choices.consequence: “Love her” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Heart.
There is no taking “Love her at distance” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: You almost kiss him. Melanie defends you publicly to the town.

choices.consequence: “Apologize to Melanie” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.
“Stay silent” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Pride.

nodes.text: She falls from her pony. Rhett breaks.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honor.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: She makes you promise to care for Ashley.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Promise” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Honest.

nodes.text: Ashley, holding Melanie's hand, weeps for Melanie, not you.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Truth—follows you into whatever comes next.
There is no taking “Look away” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Frankly, my dear, he does not give a damn.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Beg him” back. Spirit shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Let him go” back. Pride shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: You return to Tara. You rebuild. You become, in time, the woman the town respects more than likes. You die at Tara, ancient, in a field full of tomorrows.
You find Rhett, eventually. You apologize properly. He, slowly, comes around. You live, in the end, what you should have been living all along.

You build a business. You travel. You marry, late, a man who is, finally, not a project. You realize at sixty you were trying to win an argument with a younger version of yourself. You forgive her. You forgive everyone.
